# TimelineGroup { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup(
    id=None,
    name=None,
    timelines=None,
    is_locked=False,
    meta=None,
)
```

Container for commensurable timelines.

A TimelineGroup holds timelines (or sections thereof) that are
commensurable - i.e., bijectively mapped to each other via linear
interpolation. The group is defined by a timestamp table where each
row is a boundary instant.

Between any two adjacent timestamps, all present timelines have
coordinates that can be converted via linear interpolation.

Like Timeline, a Group can be locked to prevent extension.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name      | Type                                                | Description                        |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| id        | [str](`str`)                                        | Unique identifier for this group.  |
| name      | [str](`str`) \| None                                | Optional human-readable name.      |
| is_locked | [bool](`bool`)                                      | Whether the group can be extended. |
| meta      | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | Additional metadata dictionary.    |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Create empty group
>>> group = TimelineGroup(id="my_group")
```

```python
>>> # Or create with initial timelines
>>> group = TimelineGroup(id="my_group", timelines=[dgt1, audio])
```

```python
>>> # Add a timeline
>>> group.add_timeline(dgt1)
```

```python
>>> # Add with explicit boundaries
>>> from timetoalign import IdCoordinate, TimeUnit
>>> group.add_timeline(
...     score_section,
...     start=IdCoordinate(45.0, TimeUnit.seconds, "audio:1"),
...     end=IdCoordinate(135.0, TimeUnit.seconds, "audio:1"),
... )
```

```python
>>> # Convert coordinates via timestamp lookup
>>> ts = group.get_timestamp_at(75.0, "audio:1")
>>> ts["dgt1:1"]  # -> 2437.5
```

### add_timeline { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.add_timeline }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.add_timeline(
    timeline,
    *,
    start=None,
    end=None,
    allow_extension=False,
)
```

Add a timeline (or Child) to the group.

The timeline's full extent (0 to length) becomes commensurable with
the group between the specified start and end boundaries.

This method works the same whether the group is empty or already
has timelines. For an empty group, start/end default to the
timeline's own boundaries (0 and length).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                                                                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Default    |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline        | \'Timeline\'                                                                                                                   | The timeline or Child to add. If a Child, its 0-origin extent is used. If a Timeline, its full extent (0 to length).                                                                                                                                                                                                           | _required_ |
| start           | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| [GroupTimestamp](`timetoalign.timelines.groups.GroupTimestamp`) \| None | Where this timeline's section STARTS in the group. - CoordinateSpec: Coordinate in the alignment-reference timeline - IdCoordinate: Coordinate with explicit timeline_id - GroupTimestamp: Use this existing timestamp - float: Coordinate (only if single timeline in group) - None: Use group's current start, or 0 if empty | `None`     |
| end             | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`) \| [GroupTimestamp](`timetoalign.timelines.groups.GroupTimestamp`) \| None | Where this timeline's section ENDS in the group. - Same options as start - None: Use group's current end, or timeline.length if empty                                                                                                                                                                                          | `None`     |
| allow_extension | [bool](`bool`)                                                                                                                 | If True and end extends beyond current group end, add a new end timestamp. If False (default) and group is locked, raise an error.                                                                                                                                                                                             | `False`    |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                           | Description                                         |
|--------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)     | If timeline ID already exists in group.             |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`)     | If start/end specification is ambiguous.            |
|        | [RuntimeError](`RuntimeError`) | If group is locked and extension would be required. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Add to empty group - defines initial extent
>>> group.add_timeline(dgt1)
```

```python
>>> # Add to existing group - maps to existing extent
>>> group.add_timeline(audio)
```

```python
>>> # Add partial section with explicit boundaries (using IdCoordinate)
>>> from timetoalign import IdCoordinate, TimeUnit
>>> group.add_timeline(
...     score_section,
...     start=IdCoordinate(45.0, TimeUnit.seconds, "audio:1"),
...     end=IdCoordinate(135.0, TimeUnit.seconds, "audio:1"),
... )
```

```python
>>> # Extend group with new timeline
>>> group.add_timeline(
...     extended_audio,
...     end=IdCoordinate(200.0, TimeUnit.seconds, "extended_audio:1"),
...     allow_extension=True,
... )
```

### apply_flow { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.apply_flow }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.apply_flow(
    flow,
    flow_controller,
    reference_timeline_id,
    *,
    include_children=True,
    name=None,
)
```

Unfold ALL timelines in this group via a single flow.

Uses the flow controller's repeat structure to compute section
boundaries in the reference timeline's coordinate space, then
resolves those boundaries into every other timeline's coordinates
via the group's interpolation maps. Each member is unfolded along its
own resolved played spans: a new timeline of the member's **same
concrete type** with one appended child (plus a matching named Region)
per section, in unfolded coordinates.

This is the group-level equivalent of
`timetoalign.timelines.flow.create_unfolded_timeline`, but
applied to every member at once. It shares the append-children
assembly via `unfold_via_flowmap`, so each member's children and
Regions carry the same per-section names as the single-timeline path
(repeats suffixed ``-rend2``, ``-rend3`` …).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name                  | Type                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                  | Default    |
|-----------------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| flow                  | \'Flow\'               | The computed ``Flow`` (from ``controller.compute_flow()``).                                                                                                                  | _required_ |
| flow_controller       | \'FlowControllerBase\' | The ``FlowControllerBase`` that produced the flow. Required to convert flow sections to quarter-beat coordinates.                                                            | _required_ |
| reference_timeline_id | [str](`str`)           | ID of the timeline whose coordinate space the flow is defined in (typically the score CLT).  Section boundaries are resolved here first, then mapped to all other timelines. | _required_ |
| include_children      | [bool](`bool`)         | Whether to recursively slice child timelines within each section.                                                                                                            | `True`     |
| name                  | [str](`str`) \| None   | Name for the returned group.  Defaults to ``f"{self.name} (unfolded)"``.                                                                                                     | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type              | Description                                                            |
|--------|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | A new ``TimelineGroup`` containing the unfolded timelines. Each        |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | member keeps its original timeline ID, is the same concrete type as    |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | its source, and carries one appended child and Region per section.     |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | The reference timeline additionally carries a reverse FlowMap          |
|        | \'TimelineGroup\' | (id ``"source"``) and a forward FlowMap (id ``f"forward_{flow.id}"``). |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                        |
|--------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If ``reference_timeline_id`` is not in the group.  |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If the flow controller cannot compute QB sections. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> loader = Ms3Loader.from_file("notes.tsv", "measures.tsv")
>>> controller = loader.create_flow_controller()
>>> flow = controller.compute_flow(FlowMode.default)
>>> score_group = TimelineGroup(
...     id="score", timelines=[clt1, dgt1, openscore]
... )
>>> unfolded = score_group.apply_flow(flow, controller, "clt1")
```

### convert { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.convert }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.convert(
    coordinate,
    source,
    target,
    *,
    relative_to='group',
)
```

Convert a coordinate from one timeline to another.

This is a convenience method that gets the timestamp at the source
coordinate and returns the target timeline's coordinate from it.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default    |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| coordinate  | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)    | The coordinate value to convert. Accepts a raw int/float/Fraction, a Coordinate, or an IdCoordinate. A unit-qualified coordinate is resolved by the source timeline, and an IdCoordinate must agree with ``source``. | _required_ |
| source      | [str](`str`)                                           | Source timeline ID.                                                                                                                                                                                                  | _required_ |
| target      | [str](`str`)                                           | Target timeline ID.                                                                                                                                                                                                  | _required_ |
| relative_to | [Literal](`typing.Literal`)\[\'group\', \'original\'\] | "group" - coordinate is relative to timeline's 0-origin IN THIS GROUP "original" - coordinate is relative to timeline's ORIGINAL origin                                                                              | `'group'`  |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                     | Description                                                 |
|--------|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [float](`float`) \| None | The converted coordinate, or None if target timeline is not |
|        | [float](`float`) \| None | present at this coordinate.                                 |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                           |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If source or target timeline is not in the group.     |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If coordinate is outside the source timeline's range. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> group.convert(75.0, source="audio:1", target="dgt1:1")
2437.5
```

### get_events { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_events }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_events(timeline_id=None, **kwargs)
```

Get events from all timelines in the group, concatenated.

Collects events from all member timelines (or a specific one) and
concatenates their Arrow tables into a single EventData. Each row includes a
``timeline_id`` field identifying the source timeline. A member-provided
``timeline_id`` column is discarded because group membership is authoritative.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                 | Description                                                                                                     | Default   |
|-------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) \| None | If provided, only return events from this timeline. Supports partial string and regex matching.                 | `None`    |
| **kwargs    | [Any](`typing.Any`)  | Passed through to each timeline's ``get_events()`` method (e.g., ``min_coord``, ``max_coord``, ``event_type``). | `{}`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                         | Description                                                       |
|--------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | EventData with events from all (or specified) timelines. Includes |
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | a ``timeline_id`` field and standard event fields (``start``,     |
|        | [EventData](`timetoalign.storage.EventData`) | ``end``, ``event_type``, etc.).                                   |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Get all events from all timelines
>>> df = group.get_events().to_dataframe()
```

```python
>>> # Get events from a specific timeline
>>> df = group.get_events(timeline_id="clt1").to_dataframe()
```

```python
>>> # Get events with filters
>>> df = group.get_events(
...     event_type="Note", min_coord=0.0, max_coord=100.0
... ).to_dataframe()
```

### get_timeline { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timeline }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timeline(timeline_id)
```

Get a timeline by ID.

Supports partial string and regex matching:
1. Exact match: If ``timeline_id`` matches an ID exactly, returns it.
2. Substring match: If ``timeline_id`` is a substring of exactly one ID,
   returns that timeline. If multiple match, returns the first and warns.
3. Regex match: If ``timeline_id`` is a valid regex, matches via
   ``re.search()``. Same first-match logic with warning.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type         | Description                                                   | Default    |
|-------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) | The timeline's unique identifier, or a partial/regex pattern. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description          |
|--------|--------------|----------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | The Timeline object. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                         |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If no timeline matches the pattern. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> group.get_timeline("clt1")           # Exact match
>>> group.get_timeline("notes")          # Substring match
>>> group.get_timeline(r"^score:")       # Regex match
```

### get_timestamp_at { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_at }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_at(
    coordinate,
    timeline_id=None,
    *,
    relative_to='group',
    conversion_maps=True,
)
```

Get a TimeStamp at a specific coordinate.

This is the primary coordinate resolution API for TimelineGroup.
Returns a proper TimeStamp object (same as Timeline.get_timestamp).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Default    |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| coordinate      | [CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)                   | The query coordinate. Can be: - int/float/Fraction: Raw value, timeline_id required - Coordinate: Value with unit, timeline_id required - IdCoordinate: Value with unit AND timeline_id (timeline_id param optional)                                                                                                          | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`) \| None                                                  | Which timeline the coordinate refers to. Required unless coordinate is an IdCoordinate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `None`     |
| relative_to     | [Literal](`typing.Literal`)\[\'group\', \'original\'\]                | "group" - coordinate is relative to timeline's 0-origin IN THIS GROUP          (default; e.g., "3 seconds into this group") "original" - coordinate is relative to timeline's ORIGINAL origin             (e.g., "50 seconds in the original timeline")             NOTE: Currently not implemented, reserved for future use. | `'group'`  |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | Whether to include C-Map values in timestamp. - True (default): C-Maps accessible via ts.get_unit() and ts["unit_name"] - False/None: Only timeline coordinates                                                                                                                                                               | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                          |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | TimeStamp with axis set to the input coordinate and source_id set to |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | the timeline. Access other timelines via ts["other_id"] or ts.get(). |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | Access C-Maps via ts.get_unit() or ts["unit_name"].                  |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                 |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`)     | If timeline_id is not in the group.                         |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If coordinate is outside the timeline's range in the group. |
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If timeline_id is None and coordinate is not IdCoordinate.  |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> ts = group.get_timestamp_at(75.0, "audio:1")
>>> ts.axis
75.0
>>> ts["dgt1:1"]
2437.5
>>> ts.get_unit(TimeUnit.seconds)  # C-Map conversion
75.0
```

```python
>>> # Using IdCoordinate (timeline_id extracted automatically)
>>> coord = IdCoordinate(75.0, TimeUnit.seconds, "audio:1")
>>> ts = group.get_timestamp_at(coord)
>>> ts.axis
75.0
```

### get_timestamp_of { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_of }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamp_of(event_id)
```

Get the TimeStamp for a specific event by its ID.

Searches all timelines in the group for the event and returns
the corresponding TimeStamp (same structure as Timeline.get_timestamp).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type         | Description                    | Default    |
|----------|--------------|--------------------------------|------------|
| event_id | [str](`str`) | The event's unique identifier. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                | Description                                                   |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | TimeStamp at the event's coordinate, with access to all       |
|        | [TimeStamp](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.TimeStamp`) | timelines via ts["timeline_id"] and C-Maps via ts.get_unit(). |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                                |
|--------|------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If the event is not found in any timeline. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> ts = group.get_timestamp_of("note:000001")
>>> ts["audio"]  # Get coordinate on audio timeline
45.5
>>> ts.get_unit(TimeUnit.seconds)  # C-Map conversion
45.5
```

| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`) | Whether to include C-Map fields from member timelines. - True (default): Include all attached C-Maps from all timelines - False/None: No C-Map fields | `True`    |

### get_timestamps_at { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamps_at }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamps_at(
    coordinates,
    timeline_id,
    *,
    conversion_maps=True,
    units=True,
)
```

Get timestamps at multiple coordinates - the batch version of get_timestamp_at.

This is the DEAD-SIMPLE API for batch coordinate transfer: pass a sequence of
coordinates and get back a DataFrame with one field per timeline and per C-Map.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                                 | Description                                                                                                                                  | Default    |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| coordinates     | [Sequence](`typing.Sequence`)\[[CoordinateSpec](`timetoalign.core.CoordinateSpec`)\] | Sequence of CoordinateSpec to query.                                                                                                         | _required_ |
| timeline_id     | [str](`str`)                                                                         | Which timeline the coordinates refer to.                                                                                                     | _required_ |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)                | Whether to include C-Map fields from member timelines. - True (default): Include all attached C-Maps - False/None: Only timeline coordinates | `True`     |
| units           | [bool](`bool`)                                                                       | If True (default), append units to field names.                                                                                              | `True`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                                                              |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | DataFrame with one row per coordinate, one field per timeline and C-Map. |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> # Get timestamps at multiple score positions
>>> coords = [0.0, 100.0, 200.0, 400.0]
>>> df = group.get_timestamps_at(coords, "clt1_score")
>>> df.columns
Index(['clt1_score (quarterbeats)', 'dgt_holes (pixels)', ...])
```

### get_timestamps_of { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamps_of }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.get_timestamps_of(event_ids)
```

Get timestamps for multiple events.

Searches all timelines in the group for each event and returns
a DataFrame with coordinates on all timelines.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type                                          | Description                   | Default    |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|------------|
| event_ids | [Sequence](`typing.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] | List of event IDs to look up. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                                            |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | DataFrame with one row per event, indexed by event_id. |
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | Fields are timeline IDs with their coordinates.        |
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | Events not found have NaN values.                      |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> df = group.get_timestamps_of(["note:000001", "note:000002"])
>>> df.columns
Index(['clt1', 'audio', 'dgt1'])
```

### remove_timeline { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.remove_timeline }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.remove_timeline(timeline_id)
```

Remove a timeline from the group.

Updates timestamp table to remove the timeline's field.
Rows where all remaining timelines have null are removed.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type         | Description                   | Default    |
|-------------|--------------|-------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_id | [str](`str`) | ID of the timeline to remove. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description           |
|--------|--------------|-----------------------|
|        | \'Timeline\' | The removed timeline. |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                   | Description                         |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------------------|
|        | [KeyError](`KeyError`) | If timeline_id is not in the group. |

### to_dataframe { #timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup.to_dataframe }

```python
timelines.TimelineGroup.to_dataframe(
    timeline_filter=None,
    conversion_maps=True,
    *,
    fields=None,
    units=True,
    format='pandas',
)
```

Generate timestamps as a pandas DataFrame with formatted field names.

This is the recommended high-level method for getting timestamp data.
It builds on get_timestamp_table() and applies field formatting.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Default    |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| timeline_filter | [set](`set`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None                                      | Only include these timelines as fields.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `None`     |
| conversion_maps | [ConversionMapsSpec](`timetoalign.core.timestamp.ConversionMapsSpec`)     | Whether to include C-Map fields from member timelines. - True (default): Include all attached C-Maps - False/None: No C-Map fields                                                                                                               | `True`     |
| fields          | \'ColumnNaming \| Callable\[\[str, dict\], str\] \| list\[str\] \| None\' | How to name the DataFrame fields. Options: - None or ColumnNaming.name (default): Use timeline/cmap name - ColumnNaming.id: Use timeline/cmap id - Callable: Function taking (name, metadata_dict) -> new_name - list[str]: Explicit field names | `None`     |
| units           | [bool](`bool`)                                                            | If True (default), append units to field names like "name (unit)".                                                                                                                                                                               | `True`     |
| format          | [str](`str`)                                                              | Output format. Currently only "pandas" is supported.                                                                                                                                                                                             | `'pandas'` |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                                          |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | pandas DataFrame with:                               |
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | - Fields named according to the ``fields`` parameter |
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | - Units appended if ``units=True``                   |
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | - Integer fields using pandas nullable Int64 dtype   |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> df = group.to_dataframe()
>>> df.columns
Index(['audio (seconds)', 'dgt1 (pixels)', 'pixels_to_beats (beats)'])
```

```python
>>> # Without units in field names
>>> df = group.to_dataframe(units=False)
>>> df.columns
Index(['audio', 'dgt1', 'pixels_to_beats'])
```
